stem.en: Kabir asks why cancer "is mostly a disease of older people, if it starts from one cell". What piles up with time?

text.en: Mutations, from VI.4, in dividing cells. Each division risks a slip, and it takes several separate faults in one cell line, in stop receptors, in checks, in sticking, before a rogue can grow and spread. The chance that one cell has collected them all rises with the years.

feedback.en: Weak cells divide less, not more. It is the accumulation of faults, not weakness.

text.en: Older bodies have fewer stop signals.

feedback.en: The signals are there. The rogue cannot hear them.
A few cancers follow a virus, but most begin with a body's own cell going deaf.

explanation.en: Several faults must land in one cell line. Divisions accumulate them. Time accumulates divisions.
